source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Front Suspension, p.3-6

procedures.title: Toe-in: adjust
steps: Equipment that reads each wheel separately: put the steering gear on its high point, mark the 12 o'clock position on the steering shaft and set the steering wheel straight ahead.
Then loosen the clamp bolts at both ends of each tie rod and set the total toe-in to specification.
Tram gauge method: point the front wheels straight ahead.
Loosen the clamp bolts on one tie rod and set toe-in to specification.
Loosen the other tie rod's clamp bolts; turn both rods equally in the same direction to bring the steering gear to its high point with the steering wheel straight ahead.
After adjusting (Corvette): turn the inner tie rod clamps so the bolt is horizontal and below; turn the outer clamps so the bolt is vertical and toward the rear.
notes: Clamp positions for Chevrolet, Chevelle, Chevy II and Camaro differ and are omitted here.
The final 'tighten' step is implied by the loosen steps; torque values are in the Specifications.

procedures.title: Riding height and coil spring sag: check
steps: Park on a smooth level floor; bounce and rock the front end several times, lift it, then let it settle to normal height.
Take the two measurements shown in figure 8 of the manual (continued on next page).
notes: Figure 8 includes a 'Chevrolet and Corvette' view: measure from the floor to the lower control arm inner pivot and from the floor to the knuckle boss.
